clue.text: Visiting female suspect I accuse, those people brave hostile reception

indicators.note: those people are visiting, so they go inside the shuffled letters
suspect as an adjective means dubious, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

parts.note: those people means them

explanation.surface: A woman under suspicion is accused, and a group of people are bracing themselves for an angry crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspect' rearranges I ACCUSE into ACEUSIC, and 'Visiting' puts the people inside that, splitting it after its third letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To face the music is an idiom for confronting criticism or punishment, bravely accepting the consequences.

clue.text: Tone of Dutch hospital occasionally found wanting

indicators.note: only occasional letters survive, every other one being missing, so the even letters are kept

explanation.surface: Something about a Dutch hospital's character is sometimes judged inadequate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like a link word, but its F starts the run of alternate letters: oF dUtCh HoSpItAl.
explanation.definitionFit: Fuchsia is a vivid purplish-pink shade, a colour tone named after the flowering plant.

clue.text: Small part of revolutionary poem acclaimed

indicators.note: revolutionary says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A short passage from a celebrated poem about revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a description of the poem but tells you to turn OEMAC, found across 'poem acclaimed', backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as a modifier, cameo describes something brief and minor, like a cameo role or appearance.

clue.text: Picked up flat stitch in bride's clothing

indicators.note: picked up as by the ear, so the answer sounds like these words spoken

parts.note: flat means true (perfectly level, as in a true surface) and stitch means sew

explanation.surface: Someone collected a flat stitch on a wedding dress.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUE SEW said aloud gives the sound of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the collection of clothes and linen a bride assembles for her marriage.

clue.text: Issue of tennis umpire's call that's overturned

indicators.note: a call that is overturned is flipped over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tennis umpire calls time to restart play after a break

explanation.surface: A dispute arises over an umpire's decision being overruled at a tennis match.
explanation.walkthrough: In tennis the umpire calls 'Time' when a break ends; 'overturned' plays on a decision being reversed on review.
explanation.definitionFit: To emit is to issue or send out, as a sound or light is given off.

clue.text: Disconcerted athlete heading off, very embarrassed outwardly

indicators.note: the athlete's head, its first letter, comes off

parts.note: a runner is an athlete

indicators.note: only the outside letters of the following word are used

explanation.surface: An athlete pulls up, rattled and red-faced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like the athlete setting out, but it removes the first R; 'outwardly' takes ED, the outer letters of 'embarrassed'.
explanation.definitionFit: Unnerved means rattled, robbed of composure, which is what being disconcerted is.

clue.text: This writer's describing southern student finding religion

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line round, so one part encircles the other

parts.note: this writer is the setter, I, and writer's is short for writer is: I AM
L is the learner plate letter, standing for a student

explanation.surface: The setter says they are writing about a student from the south who discovers faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means drawing round, so I AM goes around S and L.
explanation.definitionFit: Islam is the monotheistic faith revealed through the Prophet Muhammad, one of the world's major religions.

clue.text: Come across party animals filling Tenerife on vacation

indicators.note: the party animals fill the space between letters
vacated, emptied of its inner letters, leaves only the outer ones

parts.note: ravers are people who love wild parties

explanation.surface: Revellers pack out Tenerife on their holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' sounds like a holiday, but it empties Tenerife down to its outer letters, and 'filling' puts the party animals between them.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to cross from one side to the other, to come across a space.

clue.text: Jersey is foggy

definitions.meaning: a knitted woollen jersey or jumper
vague or muddled, as foggy thinking is

explanation.surface: Jersey, the Channel Island, is shrouded in mist.
explanation.walkthrough: Jersey is one of the Channel Islands, but here it is a knitted pullover.
explanation.definitionFit: A woolly is British for a sweater, and woolly thinking is confused and unclear.

clue.text: Firm proposal to employ Mike brings excitement

parts.note: CO is short for company, a firm

indicators.note: to employ is to take on, so the proposal takes the letter in

parts.note: a motion is a proposal put to a meeting
Mike is the radio alphabet word for M

explanation.surface: A company's plan to hire someone called Mike causes a stir.
explanation.definitionFit: A commotion is a noisy disturbance or bustle, a state of excitement and agitation.

clue.text: Love new finale to great slow orchestral movement

indicators.note: the word gets a new last letter in place of its old one

parts.note: large means great
love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone loves the fresh ending to a great piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new finale to' swaps the last letter E of LARGE for O.
explanation.definitionFit: Largo is the Italian tempo marking for very slow, and names a movement played at that pace.

clue.text: Barely embraces partner

indicators.note: barely here means bared, stripped of its outer covering letters

parts.note: espouses means embraces, as a cause

explanation.surface: Someone hugs their other half with hardly any clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' looks like a modest adverb but strips the first and last letters off ESPOUSES.
explanation.definitionFit: A spouse is a husband or wife, one's partner in marriage.

clue.text: Instinctive pressure on old tennis star (entertaining male one) to make comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means coming back, so the letters run backwards
one who entertains a guest holds them inside

parts.note: Rod Laver, the Australian champion of the 1960s
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Pressure builds on a veteran tennis player, hosting a man, to stage a comeback.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entertaining' puts M and I inside LAVER to give LAVEMIR, which 'to make comeback' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: Primeval means primitive and elemental, so primeval urges are instinctive ones.

clue.text: Close to tea, Australian state initially adding runs after English reply

indicators.note: runs comes after English, so its letter follows
the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: NSW are the initials of New South Wales
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: At teatime in an Australian state, runs are added after England's response in a cricket match.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket breaks for tea; R is runs on a scorecard.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a reply, the response given to a question or message.

clue.text: Anxious having succeeded getting promotion into cushy job

indicators.note: a promoted letter moves up, nearer the front of the word

parts.note: insecure means anxious and lacking confidence
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in family trees

explanation.surface: A nervous person, having succeeded, gets moved up into an easy post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting promotion' moves the S of INSECURE up one place.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinecure is a post bringing pay or status but requiring little or no work.

clue.text: Greatly disturbed over husband showing sluggishness

indicators.note: the jumbled letters lie over, covering on both sides, the single letter
disturbed letters are knocked out of their order

explanation.surface: Someone is deeply upset about a husband who is idle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' rearranges GREATLY into LETARGY, which goes 'over' H.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is a lack of energy, a state of drowsy sluggishness.

clue.text: Wild dishonest types putting pleasure first

indicators.note: wild letters run free out of order and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Reckless liars who prioritise enjoyment.
explanation.definitionFit: Hedonists are people who make the pursuit of pleasure their highest goal.

clue.text: Rush and impress newspaper boss with energy

parts.note: to stamp is to impress a mark on something
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Hurry, and wow the energetic editor of a paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A stampede is a sudden headlong rush of a herd or crowd.

clue.text: Carries out works sacrificing professional's place for study

indicators.note: sacrificing means giving up one part of the word
the other piece takes the place of the part given up

parts.note: products are things produced, works
PRO is short for a professional
to con is an old word meaning to study or learn

explanation.surface: Someone carries out jobs, giving up a professional role in order to study.
explanation.walkthrough: CON for study is an archaic sense, still common in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: To conduct is to carry out or manage an activity, such as a survey.

clue.text: Compel business to make 2,000 redundant

indicators.note: making staff redundant means losing them, so these letters go

parts.note: commerce is business and trade
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so two of them are 2,000

explanation.surface: A company forces 2,000 job losses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is a link; 'redundant' removes MM from COMMERCE.
explanation.definitionFit: To coerce is to force someone to act, using threats or pressure.

clue.text: Reluctantly, perhaps, Victor tucks into processed bread

indicators.note: tucking into means going inside, so the letter is put within
processed food is altered, so these letters are reworked

parts.note: Victor is the radio alphabet word for V

explanation.surface: A man called Victor hesitantly eats some factory-made bread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' suggests eating, but it puts V inside ADERB, the rearranged BREAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Reluctantly is an example of an adverb, a word modifying a verb; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Polish upset over extremists escaping authority in country

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, read backwards

parts.note: to rub is to polish

indicators.note: the extremes of the word, its end letters, escape and are lost

parts.note: a pundit is an expert, an authority

explanation.surface: A Polish dissident, with extremists on the loose, overturns authority in a country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' is capitalised to suggest the nationality. 'upset' reverses RUB, and 'extremists escaping' strips PUNDIT to UNDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Burundi is a small landlocked nation in East Africa.

clue.text: Dance that's said to attract attention?

definitions.meaning: a dance where partners may be cut in on
the phrase used politely to get someone's attention

explanation.surface: A dance named after a polite way of catching someone's eye.
explanation.walkthrough: An excuse-me is an old-fashioned ballroom dance in which one may cut in to take another's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is a polite apology for interrupting, and also names a dance where cutting in is allowed.

clue.text: Take measurement around middle of chest

indicators.note: the measurement goes around the central letter

parts.note: size is a measurement

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: A tailor measures someone round the middle of their chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle of chest' gives E, which SIZE goes 'around'.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize is to take hold of something suddenly and forcibly.

clue.text: Hard to follow African politicians or TV presenter

indicators.note: Hard comes to follow the politicians, so its letter goes after them

parts.note: the ANC is the African National Congress, South Africa's governing party
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: It is hard to keep up with African politicians, or with a television host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'or' is not a link: its letters end the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is the main presenter who links a news or current affairs programme.

clue.text: Reportedly excellent masterstroke to produce short verse form

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so this is how it sounds

parts.note: excellent means high-quality, high, and a masterstroke is a coup, said koo

explanation.surface: Word has it that a brilliant move led to a brief poem.
explanation.walkthrough: HIGH COUP said aloud matches the answer, since coup is pronounced without its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A haiku is a three-line Japanese poem of seventeen syllables, a very brief verse form.

clue.text: Region Myanmar easily covers

indicators.note: the words cover, enclose, the letters inside them, across the gap

explanation.surface: Myanmar comfortably spans a part of the world.
explanation.definitionFit: An area is a region or district, a part of a larger space.

clue.text: Buckingham Palace insider, my good source of information

parts.note: cor is an exclamation of surprise, like my!

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it begins, its first letter

explanation.surface: An informant inside the palace is a great find for a journalist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my' is the exclamation, as in 'my, my!'. The late Queen's corgis lived at Buckingham Palace, the monarch's London home.
explanation.definitionFit: Corgis, the Welsh dog breed, were famously kept by Queen Elizabeth II and lived inside the royal palace.

clue.text: Illinois sergeant retires, concealing departure

indicators.note: retires says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue words conceal the letters within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A police sergeant in Illinois steps down while covering up their exit.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'concealing departure' as the definition, leaving the hidden-word step with no indicator; 'concealing' signals it, and 'retires' reverses NOISSERGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Egression is the act of going out, an exit or departure.

clue.text: Indefinable quality journalist illustrated originally about Oasis and Queen performing

indicators.note: about means in a disordered state, signalling rearrangement
performing letters are put through their paces in a new order
originally means at the origin, so the first letters

explanation.surface: A journalist's illustrated piece on Oasis and Queen playing live.
explanation.walkthrough: Oasis and Queen look like the bands but supply their letters, with J and I, for 'about' and 'performing' to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: The French phrase, literally I don't know what, describes an elusive quality that can't be pinned down.
